extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, reformers, and policymakers interested in American political economy, labor, and education
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidelines and evaluative principles for national political/economic reform, labour organization, and the role of education in fostering individual character and democratic purposes. Focuses on how collective experiments and institutional changes educate the nation and liberate individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough-going organization of labor
rubrics_metrics.description: The success of proposed reforms depends on 'the extent to which the thorough-going organization of labor was carried.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unions should aim to organize labor comprehensively so that efficient workers can secure rewards and less competent workers are guided into appropriate trades; if unions take full possession of fields they may create tendencies toward monopoly. The fewer trades available to non-union workers, the more unionization becomes virtually compulsory; unions must balance raising standards with avoiding pernicious monopolies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent competition by poorer/less competent laborers
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be 'a systematic attempt to prevent the poorer and less competent laborers from competing with those of a higher grade and hindering the latter's economic amelioration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory or organizational measures should create sufficient variety of work (e.g., shifting workers between trades) so that standards are maintained without permanently excluding people from all employment; but beware that partial possession of the field by unions can concentrate non-union labor into degrading trades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate supply of labor and increase its efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulating the supply of labor and increasing its efficiency will stabilize labor markets, reduce rural-urban flux, and assist agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If labor supply is made less fluid and more efficient, agricultural laborers won't flee to towns in prosperity (preventing later wage suppression in organized trades). Farm laborers are on the whole more wholesome and may prosper more in agricultural settings due to lower cost of living; regulation should thus aim to make labor abundant, stable, and comparatively efficient to enable intensive farming.

rubrics_metrics.name: State appropriation of monopoly fruits for public purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: As capital combines and corporations appropriate special franchises, 'the state is bound to appropriate the fruits of its monopoly for public purposes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When corporations are lessees of state franchises and capital combination is economically necessary, political pressure can legitimately be used to appropriate monopoly gains for public ends and to promote systematic organization of labor; this ties corporate regulation, institutional reform, and labor organization into an organic policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive national programme: realistic methods toward democratic ends
rubrics_metrics.description: A constructive national programme uses realistic, practical proposals that may be moderate in means but revolutionary in implication — unsettling habits and transforming ideas toward democratic aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measures that exploit existing tendencies and institutions can be justified as steps toward broad moral and social improvement; the programme must be national in scope and aim to realize American association without destroying national integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as primary vehicle for individual and social improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is 'the real vehicle of improvement' and is the primary way to raise human nature more surely than legal/institutional tinkering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should discipline will and intelligence, leaven social substance, and enable individuals to make illuminating use of life experience. Caution: do not over-rely on superficial, subsidized efforts (lectures, prizes, public bequests) as substitutes for formative educational processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: National education consists chiefly in experimental collective action aimed at the collective purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation's schooling is 'chiefly in experimental collective action aimed at the realization of the collective purpose,' not merely lecture halls or libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective experiments and public policies must be deliberately directed at the democratic ideal to have educative force; actions untied to the collective purpose teach little even when successful, whereas purposeful experiments teach much even through mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual education should prepare will and intelligence to make illuminating use of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual's education should 'fit him both for fruitful association with his fellows and for his own special work' by training will and intelligence to interpret and profit from personal experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education's essential purpose is to make experience real and illuminating through disinterested intelligence; second-hand experience has little value unless it illuminates one's own practical life and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine individuality arises from pursuit of a disinterested exclusive purpose and excellence of work
rubrics_metrics.description: A genuine individual 'possess[es] some special quality' achieved by the 'absorbing and exclusive pursuit' of some purpose, producing excellence in work rather than mere acquisitive success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuality is moral and intellectual: it is developed by zeal and skill in pursuing an exclusive interest (not necessarily unique), identification with one's task, and striving for excellence even when financial returns are not immediate. Acquisitive motives alone produce quantitative distinctions (bigger/smaller) rather than true individual distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: National and individual education should parallel and supplement each other
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes of national and individual education should 'parallel and supplement each other' so that individual effort contributes to national construction and national action offers formative public service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals can aid national education by single-minded pursuit of particular purposes; the nation aids individuals by offering formative, inspiring opportunities for public service. Both spheres must reinforce each other to realize the democratic promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/economic reorganization's chief value is educative and indicative of national good faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond practical results, reorganization signals 'a popular realization' and the nation's willingness to educate itself up to necessary standards; the decision to experiment may do more educatively than specific measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms should be judged also by their ability to convert public opinion to a constructive educational theory of democracy; their indirect educational value (moral and intellectual emancipation) can exceed immediate material benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superficial educational machinery must digest results of genuine experience, not substitute for it
rubrics_metrics.description: Books, subsidies, lectures, congresses and similar 'superficial educational machinery' are valuable only if used to digest and popularize the outcomes of genuine individual and national educational experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using subsidies and lectures as substitutes for well-purposed individual and national action is ineffectual—equivalent to 'an attempt to fly in a vacuum.' Such machinery should amplify, not replace, formative collective experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient organization should put collective power at service of ablest members
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization is valuable insofar as it 'may represent a standard of performance far above that of the average individual' and puts collective power at the service of the group's ablest members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective responsibility is not merely summing individuals' imperfections; it selectively enables superior abilities to find sufficient spheres of exercise and to work toward collective responsibilities, thereby raising general standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate distribution of wealth to prevent economic individualism from undermining individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing economic individualism 'inflicts the most serious damage on American individuality'—regulating wealth distribution is necessary to free individuals from the bondage produced by unregulated economic opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlimited economic opportunity tends to standardize behavior and suppress genuine individuality (successful businessmen become very much alike). Public regulation of wealth distribution is presented as a condition for richer individual development and emancipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincere pursuit of collective purpose expands individual opportunities for edifying service
rubrics_metrics.description: When a nation 'is sincerely attempting to meet its collective responsibility,' 'the better individuals are inevitably educated into active participation in the collective task' and will find more stirring, responsible work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reforms by whether they create real opportunities for personal devotion and public service; genuine national effort invites individuals to contribute energy and unselfish devotion, enriching both personal and national education.
